exposure: maternal age (teenage ≤19 years vs. adult ≥20 years)
cohort: The study included 50 teenage mothers (≤19 years) and 50 adult mothers (≥20 years) from Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College, Ajmer.
finding: Teenage mothers demonstrated lower educational attainment, belonged to lower socioeconomic backgrounds, had reduced antenatal care utilization, and experienced worse fetal outcomes (lower mean birth weight, higher low birth weight, and more neonatal complications) compared to adult mothers.
mod_finding: Normal vaginal delivery was more common in teenage mothers (70%) compared to adult mothers (50%), while cesarean section rates were higher in adult mothers (40%) compared to teenage mothers (20%).
cross-section timing: Data was collected at the time of birth and during the neonatal period for outcomes.
birth_weight: Mean birth weight was 2.5 kg for babies of teenage mothers and 2.9 kg for babies of adult mothers.
